why_math: It works because query reformulation changes what you ask for, and by optimizing for both relevance and fairness together, you disentangle bias in the training data from bias in the retrieval ranking, making both improve at once.

why_math: It works because tables have hidden structure and semantics, and testing across many task types reveals which reasoning abilities models lack, exposing whether failures come from understanding tables or from reasoning itself.

math_plain: Score retrieval system robustness by mixing real speech with 17 types of environmental noise at varying loudness levels, then measuring rank quality degradation.
why_math: It works because noise is random variation that degrades signal, and by controlling exactly which noise and how much, you isolate what breaks retrieval from what stays robust, revealing the true weaknesses systems will face.

math_plain: Score teams of experts by modeling skill-sharing collaborations as a graph, predicting which experts work well together while removing bias toward popularity and gender.
why_math: It works because expert teamwork is relational—success flows through connections—and by mapping those connections as a network, you can score teams by their relational position rather than only individual skill, while debiasing which connections get highlighted.

math_plain: Retrieve relevant emails while withholding ones marked as containing sensitive personal information.
why_math: It works because relevance and sensitivity are two separate properties that must both be scored independently, and only returning results that rank high on relevance AND low on sensitivity lets you deliver useful information without exposing privacy.

math_plain: Catalog and standardize the naming of 143 different UI elements found on search engine results pages across six engines.
why_math: Standardized naming makes comparison possible: when everyone calls the same element by the same name, researchers can then measure which elements users need, how they're laid out, and what works across search engines.

math_plain: Train multilingual models to recognize named entities in seven under-resourced tribal languages by learning shared features across related languages.
why_math: It works because languages that share structure or script also share patterns in how entities are named, and by training on related languages together, the model learns features that transfer even when training data for any single language is tiny.

math_plain: Enrich dataset search by extracting relationships not just from metadata but directly from the data files themselves, then reranking results using those connections.
why_math: It works because metadata is incomplete, but the data itself holds semantic signals—patterns and connections—and by treating those signals as a knowledge graph, you can score datasets not only by name-match but by how they relate conceptually to what you're looking for.
